title: The Valuation Impact of SEC Enforcement Actions on Nontarget Foreign Firms

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow for the supplied appendix-only package variant; the appendix describes sample construction and reports supplemental analyses, but supplies no runnable program.

issues.description: The assigned package contains only the online appendix PDF and no executable author program, README/datasheet, or entry point; the tables and figure are reported results, not runnable code.

The appendix describes manual assembly and coding of 172 SEC enforcement events and reports firm-year coverage under Compustat and accounting accrual measures, but no machine-readable event/sample data, field definitions, complete input products and histories, code, preparation sequence, software requirements, or table/figure-to-script mapping are supplied. Source names and historical collection steps are clarification context, not independently established mandatory live raw-source routes. Data requirements and dependency closure remain undetermined.

evidence.description: Bounded package/static inventory contains one appendix PDF and no supported code entry points.
The appendix describes manual assembly of enforcement actions from legal and SEC materials, without supplying a runnable workflow or the resulting data file.
evidence.quote: This section explains the process and choices for assembling the sample enforcement actions. The starting point for my search was the litigation release and administrative proceedings archives at the SEC website.

evidence.description: Appendix describes a 172-event dataset and its event-versus-firm handling for model construction.
evidence.quote: The conversion of the 172 enforcement events into the dataset required to estimate the enforcement prediction model presented a quandary in some cases.

evidence.description: Appendix reports candidate and surviving firm-year coverage under Compustat and named accounting prediction measures; these remain context rather than verified data routes.
evidence.quote: Compustat represents the total number of candidate firms that the SEC can choose to pursue, while the Kim and Skinner (2012), Dechow et al. (2012) RSST and Dechow et al. (2012) WCAcc represent the number of firm-year observations that survive for each respective analysis.

evidence.description: The appendix includes a supplementary sample/coverage table and an enforcement prediction table, but does not identify executable table-producing scripts.
evidence.quote: Supplemental Table I: Sample and Coverage Details

evidence.description: The supplied appendix includes a scaled difference-in-differences figure for enforcement actions and private litigation.

actions.description: Request the complete author replication materials for this paper variant: runnable code and run instructions, a datasheet and the author-prepared event/sample and analysis inputs (or exact input products, fields, units and historical coverage), documented manual coding and preparation steps, execution order and software requirements, and a map from the paper and supplemental tables/figure to their producing programs. Do not independently reconstruct event coding or infer complete data requirements from the appendix source references.
steps: Obtain the author code, README/datasheet, machine-readable event/sample files, analysis input descriptions and documented manual preparation instructions for the intended release.
Confirm author-defined inputs, their required fields and periods, the mapping between event-level and firm-level observations, and the full stage order.
Map all in-scope paper and appendix outputs, including the supplementary tables and Figure I, to their author entry points.
validation: Reassess the complete data and software dependency closure against the supplied workflow, verify compatible local or public routes for each required input, and confirm every in-scope output has a documented producer.

review_notes: The frozen dependency checklist is empty. The bounded package inventory contains only the appendix PDF, so no analysis_only scope is supported by supplied code and compatible author-prepared analysis inputs.

The appendix provides sample-construction context, selected coverage facts, supplemental regression tables and a figure; its historical source references do not by themselves establish all mandatory live data dependencies or a reproducible workflow.
